note: Reviewed renames and replacements of baseline assertions (docs/testing/remote-gate.md#renames). A removed baseline id is satisfied only when every `to` id is new (absent from the baseline) and ran and passed in the candidate's same step. Ids are exactly as the receipt prints them.

entries.from: Little Martians startup does not queue occupied-link routing or concurrent link egress
entries.to: Little Martians startup does not queue occupied-link routing, concurrent link egress or stair landing clearance
entries.reason: Same test, extended to the third Little Martians startup rule (stair landing clearance) when that rule was added

entries.from: a qualifying non-Little-Martians edge world still activates both rules after the existing three
entries.to: a qualifying non-Little-Martians edge world activates the three stair-traffic rules after the existing three
entries.reason: Same test, renamed when the stair landing rule made it three stair-traffic rules instead of two

entries.from: an uploaded body stays home and the log says so
to: a world that cannot resolve a carried reference keeps the default look and says why
\#795: a carried reference is resolved for its owner, pulled only when the body can change, and worn
\#795: a refused reference (unpublished, withdrawn, policy, unreachable) keeps the default look and names the code
\#795: a carried body whose source never answers is refused body.source-slow within the deadline; the trip succeeds
\#795: a traveller in the default look arrives in it, also where an earlier visit left a carried body
entries.reason: Intended behaviour change: an uploaded body now travels as a reference (#795 A2). The old assertion (it stays home) is replaced by the travel tests: an unresolvable reference keeps the default look and says why; a resolvable one is pulled and worn; refused and slow sources keep the default look

entries.from: a tall body picnics on a blanket (0.2 m); a 0.2 m seat for eating still does not fit it
entries.to: a tall body picnics on a blanket (0.2 m), eats on a 0.1 m stool and on a 1.6 m one: no seat height is refused
entries.reason: Same test, reversed by the maintainer's direction that Souls sit on any seat a def declares whatever its height: the 0.2 m eating seat that did not fit now fits, and 0.1 m and 1.6 m seats are added

entries.from: use-check: the sit capability is blocked on a seat too high for the body, from the baked seat top
entries.to: use-check: a seat higher than the body's comfortable range is offered and sat on (\#1083)
entries.reason: Same use-check, reversed by #1083: a seat above the old comfortable range is now offered and sat on; the only remaining limit, standing reach, is covered by the new 2.05 m / 2.2 m god stool test

entries.from: use-check: every core seat suits the shortest look, and SEAT_HEIGHTS is what the library revisions store
entries.to: use-check: every core seat has a real height, and SEAT_HEIGHTS is what the library revisions store
entries.reason: Same test: with no comfortable seat range left (#1083), each core seat is checked for a real height instead of fitting the shortest look; the SEAT_HEIGHTS check is unchanged
